svg.title: Assumption Input lines Preserved condition Scope control A21 Calendar and order of choices 6226–6430 Stage data and length floors, then lengths, then entry delays; one calendar chosen before every history, cutoff, period and observable. Later enlargements are monotone and preserve earlier payments; estimates on different calendars are not combined. A22 Calibration of finite histories 6617–6819, 7504–7575 Bare parameter in a closed interval; bottom coupling ̄β at level zero; deterministic forward recipe with continuous admissible levels. Existence by the intermediate value theorem only; uniqueness within the retained recipe; no inverse shooting map is assumed. A23 Reference tori and beacons 6843–7259 Read radius r with 2r ≤w; five folded reference views; compact coupling band; orders and stage parameters, then block length, then delay. Constants are tied to fixed reference tori and are not uniform in the physical period. A24 Labels and calibrated readers 8399–8753 Simple color Lie algebra, with no connectedness of the group; finite slot family; degree and level fixed before the eventual threshold. The label reader is inverted at each fixed level; its inverse bound is not uniform in the level. A25 Free comparison hierarchy 8754–9247 Explicit Gaussian kernel on the fixed real symbol space; one exterior degree bound for all weights in detection. Statements are exact in the free comparison theory; they pass to the interacting hierarchy only by rank transfer along convergent readings. A26 Euclidean rotations 10373– 10674 Bands, window and tolerance fixed before the limit removing the outer flux; three response signs f ≥0, g ≤0, h ≥0; contact subtraction. No positivity is claimed for the six individual band readings; the unsubtracted stress pair is not asserted conserved at coincident points. A27 Scaling comparison and trace limit 13237– 13994 Selected radii rk ↓0 and scaling maps; for every sequence sn ↓0 a subsequence with a scaling family on the same table and phase; monotonicity from the positive-time spectral measure. No uniformity in the degree and no bound on the scaling maps or their inverses; the interacting theory is not asserted to be free.
